# SignTalk

> SignTalk interprets sign language from a camera in real time, translates
> between sign languages, and lets anyone train new signs themselves.

SignTalk is a real-time sign language interpreter. It reads hand landmarks
from a webcam, recognises signs, and turns them into text or speech. It also
works the other way: text in, sign language out. Any sign language can be
added by recording it — the system is not limited to a fixed vocabulary.

## What it does

- **Translator** — live sign-to-text transcription from the camera, with
  optional translation into other spoken or signed languages.
- **Trainer** — record a letter, word or phrase from several angles and add
  it to your own vocabulary.
- **Direct paste** — transcribe in the background and type into whatever text
  field currently has focus, so SignTalk works inside other applications.
- **Community database** — share trained signs, or install sets contributed
  by other people.

## Pages

- [Sign in](/): the landing page and sign-in form.
- [Create an account](/signup): registration, with email and a phone number
  used only for SMS verification codes.
- [Reset your password](/forgot-password): recovery by a six-digit code sent
  over email or SMS.

## Platforms

SignTalk runs in the browser and as a desktop application for macOS, Windows
and Linux. The desktop build is the same web application wrapped in Electron,
served locally so it works offline.

## Technical notes

- The interface is a Next.js application using the App Router and React.
- Accounts are handled by a Python backend: Argon2id password hashing,
  one-time codes delivered by email or SMS, and single-use recovery tickets.
- Recognition data is modelled as symbols with per-angle captured views, so a
  sign can be matched from the front, sides, top or bottom.
